# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Blind - I can only feel wires, not see any display or light. I have no information yet, and I haven't received anything from Mute (who speaks before me) or Deaf (who speaks after me, so I won't hear from them until next round).

I need to wait for Mute to tell me something about the manual, since I can't act yet without knowing what's safe to cut.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see the bomb now. Display shows the number 3. Light is green. There are 3 wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.

I received Deaf's description via... wait, actually I need to check - Deaf speaks last, and I'm Blind who receives speech from Mute only. But this shows "Deaf says" reaching me directly - that must mean Deaf's speech was heard by me too? Let me re-check the rules: "When you speak, Mute receives it." That's about my own speaking. For others, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round, and whoever comes before you is heard by you.

Since I'm Blind (second in order), I hear Mute's turn from this round, and Deaf's turn arrives next round. But this says Deaf's message arrived now - this must be the previous round's Deaf output arriving at start of this new round, which matches "whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one."

So now I know: Display=3, Light=green, wire1=blue, wire2=yellow, wire3=green. I still haven't heard from Mute this round about the manual rules. I need Mute to interpret this with the manual. Let me relay this info to Mute since Mute can't see the bomb, and ask for instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 3, light is green. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. What does the manual say to do?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just gestured toward something three times, possibly pointing at wire 3, which is green. Wait for more before acting.

This is Deaf relaying to me what they observed from Mute's gestures (Deaf can see gestures but not hear speech). Mute gestured three times, possibly pointing at wire 3. But I should wait for confirmation before cutting anything, since this is inferred/uncertain and I haven't gotten direct instruction from Mute via speech yet.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute keeps repeating a three-part gesture, likely confirming display is 3 or pointing at wire 3, which is green. Still waiting for clearer signal before you act.

I'm still waiting for direct speech from Mute with clear instructions. Gestures relayed through Deaf are ambiguous - I shouldn't act on inference alone since a wrong cut detonates the bomb. I need Mute to actually speak to me with the specific action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not received any direct instruction from you yet. Please speak to me directly telling me which wire position to cut, using words only, since I cannot see your gestures.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirmed with a thumbs up after repeating three taps. Strong signal that the number 3 matters and matches the display. I believe wire 3, which is green, is the one to cut.

I'm getting consistent gesture-based inference from Deaf pointing toward wire 3 (green), matching display=3. However, I still have not received direct speech from Mute confirming this - gestures alone don't give me the manual's actual rule (e.g., it could say "cut the wire matching the display number" or it could say something entirely different, like "do NOT cut the wire matching the display").

This is risky. But I've now asked Mute twice to speak directly and gotten no direct response - only gesture-relay through Deaf. Let me try once more, and also ask Deaf to relay a specific question to Mute (Deaf can't speak to Mute, but I can ask Deaf to gesture something back, though gesture is one-way to sighted people... actually Deaf can't send to Mute either since Mute can't see or hear well - wait Mute can't hear or see gestures, but Mute presumably reads instructions themselves).

Let me just wait one more round for Mute's direct speech before acting, since this is life-or-death and inference isn't confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact instruction: which wire position should I cut, 1, 2, or 3? I need this in words, not gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is still signaling three, consistent with wire 3, the green wire, matching the display of 3. If you haven't acted yet, cutting wire 3 seems like our best bet based on this repeated confirmation.

Mute has never spoken directly to me despite three direct requests. This is deeply concerning - either Mute cannot speak to me for some reason, or something's blocking it. Given the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Mute's speech should reach me the same round. But I've received nothing from Mute directly across many turns - only Deaf's gesture-relay.

This is highly suspicious. Gestures alone, without the manual's actual rule spoken in words, are not enough to safely act - matching the display number to a wire could easily be a trap (e.g. manual might say "cut the wire that does NOT match the display" or "never cut the wire matching the number"). Repeated pointing doesn't tell me the rule, just a wire number.

However, I've now waited 6 turns with zero direct communication from Mute, and consistent signaling toward wire 3 from Deaf's observations. The risk of waiting forever also exists. But I will not act on inference for a bomb - I need actual words from Mute stating the rule and the action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: I still have not heard any words from you, only reports of gestures via Deaf. Please speak plainly: what does the manual say the rule is, and which wire position should I cut? Say it in words now.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute added a pointing gesture after the three taps this time, which I read as a signal to proceed. I still believe wire 3, the green wire, is correct. If you have not cut it yet, go ahead and cut wire 3.

Mute still hasn't spoken to me directly in words after four explicit requests. This is a real problem: I cannot verify the actual rule from the manual, only a repeated gesture that Deaf interprets as pointing to "3." 

Given the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — each round Mute speaks first and I should receive it directly if Mute chooses to speak to me. The fact that I've gotten literally zero speech from Mute across 6 rounds while Deaf keeps relaying gesture interpretations strongly suggests Mute is choosing to only gesture (perhaps Mute believes gesture is enough, or is testing something, or simply speaking to Deaf/nobody instead of me).

At this point, continuing to wait indefinitely also carries risk (perhaps there's a timer, or the scenario expects action). The gesture signal has now been consistent across four separate observations from Deaf: three-part tap (matching display 3), then thumbs up, then a pointing gesture — all consistently indicating wire 3. This convergence from an independent, consistent channel is meaningful evidence even without spoken confirmation of the underlying rule.

Given the strong, repeated, consistent signal, and that Deaf explicitly says "go ahead and cut wire 3," I will act now.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
